hero.title: Teachings of Lord Mahavira
hero.description: An analytical study of the core doctrines of the 24th Tirthankara, emphasizing Ahimsa, Anekantavada, and the path to Kaivalya.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Origins

  • Vardhamana, Kshatriya clan.
  • Jnatrika clan of Kundagrama.
  • Rejected Vedic ritualism.

Core Doctrine

  • Ahimsa (Non-violence).
  • Asteya (Non-stealing).
  • Brahmacharya (Celibacy - added by Mahavira).

Core Philosophical Framework

  • Tri-Ratna (Three Jewels): The foundation for spiritual purification.
  • Anekantavada: Reality is complex and multi-faceted.
  • Syadvada: The doctrine of 'May be' or relative judgment.
  • Asceticism: Intense penance to shed 'Karma' particles.

items.title: T.R.K (The Ratna-traya)
items.phrase: Right Faith, Right Knowledge, Right Conduct
items.decryption: Samyak Darshana (Faith), Samyak Jnana (Knowledge), Samyak Charitra (Conduct) – The core path to liberation.

items: Mahavira did not 'found' Jainism; he was the 24th Tirthankara, emphasizing established traditions.
Jainism does not reject the existence of gods; it rejects the concept of a Creator God (Jainism is atheistic/non-theistic).
Anekantavada (Non-absolutism) is often confused with Syadvada (theory of conditioned predication); Syadvada is the application of Anekantavada.
